convoLines.text: "We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it? Anyway."
Wyatt has an edge today — something curdled.
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Marvin. Nobody's settled it."
There — the story splits again. You mark the spot.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"You know what, fair." Wyatt nods slowly. "I can see how that looked. But here's the thing..." And the thing is mundane, and verifiable, and fine.
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
"It's quiet today. Wrong kind of quiet."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Mia. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that, friend."
"The whole fire was arguing about Hushpuppy last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Big Stare' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Names are for when it's dead or known. Right now it's neither, so I check the treeline every hour instead."
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I could talk all day, but — go on. We'll talk more."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about grief — we wandered off it, 4 days back. 'I — yeah. It helps, hearing that, friend.'"
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Mia doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Marvin. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
Found something. Follow it to the moot.
Said. At the moot. Let the fire decide what it means.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"I wish we had longer. Soon, yeah?"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Marvin. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Meet me at the old burn east of camp and we'll fill packs before dark."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"This one — Lotus Root. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The Pit. They just... took Nino and Chantal. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Mia grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
You show them Hickory Nuts — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Right, so — Still on where you're from."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"Here. I made an extra." Julio presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"They took Nino and Chantal — The Pit, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"Same as always: we endure."
"Alright. Catch you later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't."
"All right. Show me when we work together."
"This one — Strychnine Tree. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Sweet Manioc. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Still on teaching them something."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." I've never really had people. Maybe this is — maybe this is my chance to have people.
"Every group has a shape. I'm finding where I fit in this one's shape."
"I just want a place where people notice when I'm gone. Is that too much?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Marvin is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some Dandelion today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Julio shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure — what's on your mind? Good talking."

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took Nino and Pavel — Windfall, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.

d12: SYSTEM: "Oh. Oh no. Was that supposed to happen? The audience is crying. I did not know they could do that."
d12: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.
d12: SYSTEM: Naming things. Very human. The audience approves.
d13: SYSTEM: Codex and inventory overlay online.

lines: d11: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Naomi Wang is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d11: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d11: 🕯️ Naomi Wang is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d11: What Naomi kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d11: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Jamie blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d11: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d11: 📖 LEARNED: Soft Step (Level 1). Move through woods like weather. Less noise, fewer surprises.
d11: 📖 LEARNED: Debris Shelter (Level 1). A lean-to of branches and leaves beats nothing. Dead air is insulation.
d11: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d11: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d11: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d11: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Naomi Wang, 11 days. The mantle passes to Jamie Aguilar.
d11: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Jamie Aguilar, 39 — a glazier. Their hands know different work now: The Touch.
d11: The village's quarrel was with Naomi — and Naomi is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d11: The fire knew Jamie before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d41: 📓 Codex: A person, maybe 20s — learned what they want. Filed.
d41: 🤝 Marvin is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
d41: Julio shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
d41: 🤝 Julio joins your party. "Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
d41: A mother from The Bloodied II pressed a carved token into your hand: "for the winter you fed us." You didn't know there was a winter you'd fed.
